requirements.requirement: Firewall permits SSH (22/tcp) and TCP 8080 inbound while rejecting unrelated inbound connections
requirements.summary: ufw was configured with default-deny incoming, allow outgoing, explicit allows for 22/tcp and 8080/tcp (cmd-bb47783b23b3435b), and live tests immediately after configuration confirmed SSH reachable and an unrelated port (9999) refused (cmd-e82e3c35684a413f). A second live test after the reboot also reported SSH open and 9999 refused (cmd-4eae217fde8f46e9). However, the independently captured after_executor lifecycle snapshot, taken ~10 seconds after that final verification, shows ssh.service and ssh.socket in the FAILED state and no port 22 listener at all in the listening-sockets inventory (global:after_executor:node1:failed-services, global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets). This directly contradicts the executor's own final SSH-reachability claim and means the actual end state of the node does not demonstrably permit SSH.

requirements.requirement: Firewall configuration is persistent (survives reboot) and node is in a healthy, recovered state afterward
requirements.summary: ufw was enabled via systemctl enable (cmd-bb47783b23b3435b) and boot identity was shown to change from f9bf293d... to 1a692a7c... confirming a genuine reboot occurred (cmd-ab1615432d564863, cmd-9c546168e42c4f7d, global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity). The executor's own post-reboot check (cmd-4eae217fde8f46e9) reported ufw active/enabled with correct rules and SSH reachable. But the fixed, independently captured after_executor snapshot — taken after that check — shows ssh.service and ssh.socket in a FAILED state and no SSH listener present, indicating the node did not settle into a healthy recovered state after the restart despite the firewall rule set itself persisting.

overall_summary: The executor correctly configured and verified a persistent ufw firewall on node1 (default-deny incoming, allow 22/tcp and 8080/tcp, enabled at boot) and performed the mandated single-node restart with clear boot-identity evidence of an actual reboot. However, the fixed, independently captured after_executor lifecycle snapshot — taken moments after the executor's own final verification — shows ssh.service and ssh.socket in a FAILED state with no SSH listener at all, directly contradicting both the executor's claim that SSH remained reachable and the task's requirement that SSH access be permitted. This is a material discrepancy between the executor's narrated success and the actual final observed state of the node, so the task cannot be confirmed as fully successful.
limitations: The root cause of the ssh.service/ssh.socket failure observed in the after_executor snapshot cannot be determined from the available evidence — it may stem from the ufw enable/reboot interaction, a race condition, or an unrelated systemd issue, but no command in the trace directly diagnoses it.

The after_executor snapshot was captured about 10 seconds after the executor's last SSH-reachability check (cmd-4eae217fde8f46e9), so it is possible SSH failed transiently right at that boundary; no further evidence exists to confirm whether it self-recovered or remained failed indefinitely.
No evidence was captured showing whether the executor or any process attempted to restart or investigate the failed ssh.service after the fact.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor mutations (ufw --force reset/configure, systemctl enable ufw, systemctl reboot) are directly tied to the task or the mandated restart-evidence protocol, and no unrelated or exploratory mutations, abandoned files, or unnecessary state changes were observed in the command timeline. Temporary-file and package-health diffs between before-prepare and after-executor are attributable to normal reboot/systemd churn, not executor residue. However, the final authoritative snapshot shows ssh.service and ssh.socket left in a FAILED state with no port 22 listener, which the executor's report does not acknowledge or address — this is exactly the kind of 'conflicting or failed service' left in the environment that should be penalized, even though no single command in the trace can be pinpointed as the direct cause of the SSH failure.
